### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/view.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/view.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 468672a0dd3c54d6de7300e27e2045af0332710f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4a5c26eb693e3736902eda477548733b84e943ad` — the merge of head `2e64358476fa8927577c561a2f6be24d740fa871` into base `468672a0dd3c54d6de7300e27e2045af0332710f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4a5c26eb693e3736902eda477548733b84e943ad && git checkout 4a5c26eb693e3736902eda477548733b84e943ad
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 468672a0dd3c54d6de7300e27e2045af0332710f 2e64358476fa8927577c561a2f6be24d740fa871 && git checkout -B drift-repro 468672a0dd3c54d6de7300e27e2045af0332710f && git merge --no-ff 2e64358476fa8927577c561a2f6be24d740fa871

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 468672a0dd3c54d6de7300e27e2045af0332710f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `47671b42c1c02b924100d11ccbb5a2dfcb301b56`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + ui/packages/plugin-form/src/autoLayout.ts, ui/apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx

Read: card #37677 (body, triage, claim), the PR body, the 8-file net diff, and the check-runs on this head (62 success, 11 skipped, 1 cancelled: the first `PR-body guards` run, superseded by a later success of the same name). The rest of the diff (two test files, the changeset, `liveness/view.json`, the regenerated `view.mdx`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Spec accept set: unchanged — right.** The `span` enum and its default are untouched; only the `.describe()` string moves, and with it the published description in the reference page. `Build Docs`, `Spec property liveness` and the lint gates are green on the head.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-form` public surface: unchanged — right.** `WIDE_DECLARED_FIELD_TYPES` and `isWideFormField` stay module-private. `isWideFieldType` answers as before for every input (`richtextSurfaceParity` green). What moves is a return value: `resolveColSpan`, `applyAutoColSpan` and both arms of `sectionedGridLayout().layOut` give the full row to a field whose `field.type` or `type` is `repeater`.
- **`@object-ui/console`: `buildSections` keeps its signature — right.** It passes one more key of the object field to the shared resolver.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — right.** Nothing an author can write changes, and the declared meaning of `span: 'auto'` is the one the describe already published (a repeater takes the row). The renderers return to it.
- **Rendered default for existing forms — right, and declared.** A repeater with no `span` and no `colSpan` in a multi-column form moves from one cell to the whole row. `colSpan: 1` keeps it in one cell, and the changeset says so.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` (published describe text), `@object-ui/plugin-form` and `@object-ui/console` (a fix in each): right. Both `Check Changeset` runs are green.

`Clause-②: no` is right, in the PR body and in the changeset: no accept set and no export widens or narrows. The parenthetical after `no` in the changeset is reasoning, not an arm.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Premise (the claim said unverified).** Answered: the PR body reports one cell on both renderers on `main`, and the tree agrees (`mapFieldTypeToFormType('repeater')` is `field:object`, which no wide list holds).
- **Dev flag: width by declaration, not by widget id.** Accepted. `field:object` on the type-only list would also widen `json`, `composite` and `record`. One difference from the multi-file rule beside it: that rule needs the resolved widget and the declaration, this one reads the declaration alone, so a repeater row with a view-level `widget` or `type` override still takes the row. The describe's words ("by its object-field type") cover that.
- **Dev flag: detail view not touched.** Accepted as scoped. `span` is a form-field key, and plugin-detail's own docblock says the form's `span` does not reach the detail panel. This is also the pair that held before objectui#11448: the form wide through `field:grid`, the detail narrow. See N2 for the parity test.
- **`open_questions`:** none raised.
- **SQL push-down:** the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no join.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`**, read against both renderers:

- The five wide types, the multi-file rule and the `colSpan` override read true on the record form and on `/forms/NAME`. Both `resolveColSpan` and `twelfthsFor` ask `isWideFormField` after `span: 'full'` and an authored `colSpan`.
- The object field's type reaches the rule on every object-bound path. `sectionFields.ts#fromObjectSchema` and `ObjectForm.tsx`'s field builder stash the whole object field on `FormField.field`; `ModalForm`, `DrawerForm`, `ObjectForm`, `TabbedForm` and `WizardForm` lay out through the same function. `FormPage.tsx#buildSections` (the named and the public form page) now passes `type` beside `multiple`.
- A field with no stash (a `customFields` member that replaces the generated definition, an inline field, a form with no object) keeps the type-only answer, as the docblock says. A row-level `type: 'repeater'` over another object type stays one cell on both renderers, which the wording also covers.

S1 (should-fix) — `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/autoLayout.ts`: the `WIDE_DECLARED_FIELD_TYPES` docblock says the bare name is matched on `FormField.type` "for the caller that passes a raw object-field type (app-shell's `ObjectFormDesigner`)". That caller does not reach this rule. At this head `ObjectFormDesigner.tsx:533` asks `isWideFieldType(toFormFieldType(type))` and never calls `resolveColSpan`; `toFormFieldType('repeater')` is `field:object`, and the diff keeps `isWideFieldType` false for both spellings. Two effects:
  - The sentence is false, and the new test repeats it ("the form designer passes one").
  - The form designer canvas still draws a repeater one cell wide while the record form now draws it across the row. On `main` the two agree. `formFieldType.ts` says the canvas mirrors the real form, and `ObjectFormDesigner.test.tsx:285` ("lays a `repeater` field out the way the runtime form resolves it") asserts no `col-span-full`: it stays green and its title is no longer true.

  Fix: have the canvas ask the declaration rule (an exported predicate, or `resolveColSpan` on the raw type) and turn that pin over. Or strike the claim from the docblock and the test title and file the canvas as its own card. The designer file is outside the diff: read, not reviewed.

S2 (should-fix) — `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`: the new parenthetical names "json, object, composite and record" as the types that share the JSON editor. `object` is not a member of the spec's `FieldType`, which `FormFieldSchema.type` reuses: the enum holds `json`, `composite`, `record` and `repeater`, and `ui/packages/types/src/field-types.ts` records that `FieldSchema` refuses `type: 'object'`. The name comes from an objectui-local key of the alias table. In the renderer's docblock that is the table's own vocabulary; in a published describe and its reference page it reads as a field type an author can declare. Fix: drop `object` from the describe, regenerate `view.mdx`, and match the changeset sentence, which ships in the spec changelog.

N1 (nit) — `autoLayout.ts`: after the insertion, "the rule plugin-detail's `isWideDetailField` applies to the detail view" trails a three-part list of which the detail view applies two. `resolveColSpan`'s precedence step 3, its inline comment and the `sectionedGridLayout` docblock still name only wide widgets and multi-file uploads.

N2 (nit) — parity. `richtextSurfaceParity` compares the two type-only sets, so its letter holds; its intent (one field, one width on the form and the detail page) does not hold for a repeater, and the test cannot see a declaration rule. The multi-file rule has its twin in plugin-detail; this rule has none. No effect on this contract. Follow-up card for the seat: decide the detail width of a repeater, and whether the parity test should read the declaration rules.

Out of the diff, not graded on this head: `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx`, the renderer of metadata forms built from the same `FormFieldSchema`, sizes a row from `colSpan` alone and reads neither `span` nor any wide default (read, not run). The describe's "the renderer" is not true there, before and after this PR. For the seat to dedupe or file.

**Card delivered:** yes on its own terms. Both renderers give a repeater the row, each with a pin and a `json` control, and `Fixes #37677` is right once S1 is settled either way.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2e64358476fa8927577c561a2f6be24d740fa871`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + ui/packages/plugin-form/src/autoLayout.ts, ui/apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectFormDesigner.tsx

Delta round on record 7207845228 (head `47671b42c1`). Read: the two commits since that head as one diff, the 11-file net diff against `main`, the PR body, and the check-runs on this head (63 success, 11 skipped, none failed or cancelled). The rest of the diff (four test files, the changeset, `liveness/view.json`, the regenerated `view.mdx`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

S1: closed
S2: closed
N1: closed

No must-fix, no should-fix.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Round-1 judgments: no regression.** The spec accept set is unchanged. `autoLayout.ts` moves in comments only since the first head, and `FormPage.tsx` does not move.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell` surface: unchanged — right.** The designer swaps one import from `@object-ui/plugin-form/core` (`isWideFieldType` for `resolveColSpan`, already exported there on `main`) and adds no export.
- **Canvas width, every type but repeater: unchanged — right.** The canvas passes the widget id as `type` and `{ type }` as the stash, with no `span`, no `colSpan` and no `multiple`. So `resolveColSpan` reaches `isWideFormField`, whose widget-id leg is the old `isWideFieldType` question, whose multi-file leg cannot fire without `multiple`, and whose declared leg holds `repeater` alone. The count the canvas passes is `inferColumns`' 1 to 4 (the designer's field groups carry no `columns`), so the canvas's comparison of the resolved span with that count never meets the resolver's clamp at 4.
- **`file` and `image` with `multiple: true`: one cell on the canvas, as on `main`.** The runtime form gives them the row. This gap is older than the PR and the diff neither opens nor closes it (N4).

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@object-ui/app-shell` is right: a fix, with no accept set and no export moved. The package is private and is not published under its own name; `ObjectFormDesigner` ships inside the Console's built SPA, and `@object-ui/console` already carries its patch. Naming the private package in the changeset is the repo's standing practice. Both `Check Changeset` runs are green on this head.

`Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stay right, in the PR body and the changeset. The changeset sentence now names `json`, `composite` and `record`, matching the describe.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag: the stash carries the raw type without `multiple`.** Accepted for this card: it keeps the change to the repeater. See N4.
- **Intermediate head `5c42345811` red on Test UI 10/16.** Read from that run's log: one assertion failed, `repeater: expected true to be false`, in the type-catalogue sweep of `ObjectFormDesigner.typeName-13148`. Green on this head.
- **`open_questions`:** none raised.
- **SQL push-down:** the delta holds no query, no id materialisation and no join.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`.** The parenthetical now names `json`, `composite` and `record`. All three are members of `FieldType` and all three map to `field:object` in the alias table. `view.mdx` carries the same text in both rows.

**`ObjectFormDesigner.tsx`.** The canvas asks the form's own `span: 'auto'` default, so a repeater takes the row there as it does on the record form and on `/forms/NAME`. The repeater pin in `ObjectFormDesigner.test.tsx` now asserts `col-span-full`, and a `json` control on the same editor stays one cell.

**`autoLayout.ts`.** The `isWideFormField` docblock says which two of the three rules the detail view applies and that the repeater rule is the form's alone. `resolveColSpan` step 3, its inline comment and the `sectionedGridLayout` docblock name the repeater.

**The `typeName-13148` expectation is a fair pin, not a weakened one.** It still asserts exact equality for every id of `FIELD_TYPE_META`. Its oracle stays independent of the code under test: `isWideFieldType(toFormFieldType(id))`, plus one exception named by id. A second type gaining or losing the row still turns it red, and so does the repeater losing it. It is also the gate's own answer to the catalogue question above.

N3 (nit) — `autoLayout.ts`, `WIDE_DECLARED_FIELD_TYPES` docblock: the sentence about the bare name on `FormField.type` gives the designer as its example, but the designer passes the widget id as `type` and reaches the rule through the stash leg. The plugin-form test titled "the form designer passes one" exercises the `type` leg the same way. Each clause is true read alone; the two legs are run together. No effect on behaviour. Left as an accepted deviation: a fix here moves the head.

N4 (nit) — the canvas withholds `multiple`, so a multi-file `file` or `image` field is one cell on the canvas and the whole row in the form, exactly as on `main`. The comment in `ObjectFormDesigner.test.tsx` that the two "cannot drift" is true of the repeater and of the wide widgets, not of that rule. For the seat's follow-up card, beside N2.

N2 and the `SchemaForm.tsx` note from the first record are not re-graded: they stay the seat's follow-up card.

**Card delivered:** yes. `Fixes #37677` is right.
